discovery: Discovery of strong magnetoelectric coupling in multiferroics, in which magnetic order drives and controls ferroelectricity

nominees.name: Yoshinori Tokura
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and University of Tokyo, Japan

subfield: Condensed matter physics (multiferroics and magnetoelectric materials)
motivation: In 2003, Tokura's group (TbMnO3) and Cheong's group (TbMn2O5) found that spiral magnetic order can break inversion symmetry and create electric polarization. Magnetic fields could then reverse or switch that polarization, making strong magnetoelectric coupling something experiments could study and control. In the same year, Ramesh's epitaxial BiFeO3 films showed robust room-temperature multiferroicity. He went on to demonstrate electric-field control of antiferromagnetic domains and of exchange-coupled ferromagnets. Together these results founded the field of 'type-II' multiferroics. They identified the spin-current and inverse Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya mechanisms and introduced electromagnons, a new class of collective excitation that THz and optical spectroscopy now probe directly. The ideas have since reached atomically thin van der Waals multiferroics, and they guide the search for ultralow-power magnetoelectric memory and logic. This work changed how we think about coupling spin, charge and lattice in quantum materials.
